home.hero.title:
Walking through
chemical space.
home.hero.statement: I develop machine-learning methods that bring chemical knowledge — conformations, pharmacophores, and molecular interactions — into molecular representation and drug design. My work spans small-molecule discovery and protein–ligand, protein–protein, and RNA–ligand interaction modeling, with emerging directions in phenotype-based and multi-target drug design.

Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences
home.dossier.deck: Ouroboros addresses a persistent divide in AI-driven drug discovery: representations optimized for prediction are rarely reusable for molecular design. By organizing chemical space with fingerprint, conformational-space, and pharmacophore relationships, it supports property prediction, virtual screening, and property-guided generation within one representation. This creates a common basis for hit discovery, lead optimization, and multi-target design.
home.dossier.encodeText: Conformational-space and pharmacophore relationships preserve functionally relevant neighborhoods across structurally distinct molecules.
home.dossier.navigateText: A shared representation supports property prediction, similarity-based screening, and target-oriented prioritization across discovery settings.
home.dossier.decodeText: Property objectives guide the proposal of candidates for directed optimization and targeted polypharmacology.
home.lineage.title: From recognizing cross-scaffold similarity to designing within it.
home.lineage.intro: GeminiMol showed that conformational-space and pharmacophore relationships can reveal functionally related molecules across scaffold boundaries. Ouroboros extends this concept into a shared chemical space that connects prediction with candidate design.
home.lineage.geminiText: GeminiMol prioritizes molecules with related 3D and pharmacophore profiles even when their 2D structures are dissimilar.
home.lineage.geminiValidation: Outcome cross-scaffold screening and the experimentally validated GluN1/GluN3A inhibitor GM-10.
home.lineage.ouroborosTitle: Prediction and design in one chemical space
home.lineage.ouroborosText: Ouroboros organizes several molecular relationships together so prediction and generative exploration share a chemically meaningful space.
home.lineage.ouroborosValidation: Scope property prediction, directed optimization, and targeted polypharmacology.

home.projects.title: Selected projects
home.projects.intro: Methods I led or co-led and collaborative studies I contributed to, grouped by research line. Each label states my authorship role on the primary paper.
home.projects.ouroboros.tagline: Connecting molecular prediction with property-guided design.
home.projects.ouroboros.detail: Ouroboros addresses the divide between predicting molecular properties and designing new candidates. A shared, chemically organized representation preserves conformational-space and pharmacophore relationships while supporting similarity-based screening, directed molecular optimization, and polypharmacology design.
home.projects.geminimol.tagline: Finding functional similarity beyond shared 2D scaffolds.
home.projects.geminimol.detail: GeminiMol addresses the problem that functionally similar molecules can appear unrelated in two-dimensional structure. It supports cross-scaffold property prediction, virtual screening, target identification, and scaffold hopping; screening 18 million compounds led to GM-10, an experimentally validated GluN1/GluN3A inhibitor.
home.projects.ppiminer.tagline: Finding receptor-compatible backbone motifs beyond sequence similarity.
home.projects.ppiminer.detail: PPI-Miner reveals interaction partners that sequence-motif searches can miss because unrelated proteins may preserve the local backbone geometry required for receptor recognition. In the CRBN case, it produced 1,739 candidates and recovered 16 previously reported cases; at least 12 additional candidates in the released library later received compound-dependent recruitment support.
home.projects.deepsa.tagline: Predicting synthetic accessibility for molecular design.
home.projects.deepsa.detail: DeepSA is a co-developed deep-learning model that estimates how difficult a small molecule is to synthesize. Its scores help filter computationally proposed candidates before experimental follow-up and complement other assessments during molecular design.

home.news.title: News
home.news.intro: Selected milestones from collaborative research, software releases, competitions, and publications, including the archive from the earlier site.
home.news.2026_cocobind: The CoCoBind study connects RNA–compound interaction prediction with nucleotide-level binding-site localization, supporting site-aware RNA–ligand recognition under distribution shift. It was published in Journal of Medicinal Chemistry.
home.news.2026_ouroboros: The Ouroboros study, Learned Conformational Space and Pharmacophore Into Molecular Foundational Model, was published in Advanced Science.
home.news.2024_11: The PhenoScreen project introduced a dual-space contrastive learning framework combining conformational-space and molecular-image similarities for virtual screening.
home.news.2024_09: A collaborative study using GeminiMol reported a GluN1/GluN3A inhibitor (IC50 = 0.98 μM); the project received first prize in the 2023 Shanghai International Computational Biology Innovation Competition.
home.news.2024_08: The GeminiMol paper was published in Advanced Science.
home.news.2023_12: The GeminiMol project introduced molecular representation learning informed by conformational-space similarity; see the code and bioRxiv preprint.
home.news.2023_10: DeepSA was published in the Journal of Cheminformatics; the DeepSA web server is also available.
home.news.2023_01: DeepSA, co-developed with Shihang Wang, was released as a model for estimating the synthetic accessibility of small molecules.
home.news.2022_12: The original plmd scripts were expanded and renamed AutoMD, adding support for additional force fields and configurable trajectory-analysis pipelines.
home.news.2022_11: The PPI-Miner study showed how conserved backbone motifs can reveal protein-interaction candidates even when their sequences diverge. The paper appeared in the Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling, with source code on GitHub.
home.news.2021_08a: A collaborative study reported an allosteric pocket on the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein and inhibitor candidates designed to restrict its conformational change; the paper appeared in the Journal of Medicinal Chemistry.
home.news.2021_08b: A collaborative study reported five candidate small-molecule blockers targeting the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein in Acta Pharmacologica Sinica.
home.news.2021_05: Automated Schrödinger workflows for cross-docking (XDock), virtual screening (GVSrun), and molecular-dynamics simulation (plmd) were released, with source code on GitHub.
home.news.2020_05: Biodb-Search was released as a browser-based navigator that submits one query to multiple biomedical databases.
home.news.2019_12: GetPDB was released as a script for downloading single-chain protein structures by UniProt ID.

home.news.2025_crbn: A retrospective cross-reference of the released CRBN candidate database found at least 12 candidates beyond the paper's original set of 16 that were later supported by compound-dependent CRBN-recruitment assays; mutating the predicted G-loop glycine abolished the recruitment signal (Science, 2025).
home.program.title: Bringing chemical knowledge into models of molecules, interactions, and phenotypes.
home.program.moleculesText: Chemically informed representations that recognize functional similarity across scaffolds and connect property prediction with molecular design.
home.program.interactionsText: Structure- and learning-based models of protein–protein, protein–ligand, and RNA–ligand recognition, from receptor-compatible interface motifs to nucleotide-level binding sites.
home.program.phenotypesText: Multi-target drug design within a shared chemical space and phenotype-based compound prioritization, developed as an emerging direction of the program.
home.projects.cocobind.tagline: Predicting whether and where small molecules bind RNA.
home.projects.cocobind.detail: CoCoBind treats RNA–compound interaction prediction and nucleotide-level binding-site localization as one multitask problem. Consistency-contrastive learning links the two tasks, supporting site-aware RNA–ligand recognition under distribution shift.
